about: AI-specific code and configuration rules for aiwiki_check.py. Each rule names the wiki controls it supports and the test cases that prove the fix. Rules are heuristics that prompt a reviewer; a clean result is not proof that a control is in place.

rules.title: Model output passed to code or shell execution
rules.message: Text from a model reaches eval, exec or a shell on this line.
rules.remediation: Never execute model output directly. Parse it into a fixed set of allowed actions, validate the arguments outside the model, and run any generated code in an isolated sandbox with no secrets and no network.

rules.title: Model output rendered as raw HTML
rules.message: Model output is inserted into a page without escaping, which allows script injection and link or image exfiltration.
rules.remediation: Escape model output by default. If you must render Markdown, sanitise the HTML with an allow-list and block remote images and links to unknown hosts.

rules.title: Model output built into a SQL statement
rules.message: A SQL statement is assembled from model output by string formatting.
rules.remediation: Use parameterised queries, and give the model a fixed set of query templates or a read-only role rather than free SQL.

rules.title: Model or data file loaded with unsafe deserialisation
rules.message: This load can run code embedded in the file. A model or dataset from outside your control can execute on load.
rules.remediation: Prefer safetensors or another format that cannot carry code. For torch.load pass weights_only=True explicitly (check the default for your PyTorch version). Scan third-party model files before loading and load them only from your own registry.

rules.title: Remote model code trusted at load time
rules.message: trust_remote_code runs Python shipped with the model repository on your machine.
rules.remediation: Avoid it. If a model needs it, review the code, pin the exact revision, and load it only in an isolated environment.

rules.title: Model downloaded without a pinned revision
rules.message: A hub model is fetched by name only, so a later push to that repository changes what you run.
rules.remediation: Pass revision= with a commit hash, and record the model, revision and hash in your AI-BOM.

rules.title: MCP server launched from an unpinned package
rules.message: The MCP server is started from a package with no fixed version, so a new release runs without review.
rules.remediation: Pin the exact version (or the image digest), review the server's tool definitions, and record the pin in your tool inventory.

rules.title: Remote MCP server over plain HTTP
rules.message: A remote MCP server is reached over http://, so tokens and tool results cross the network unencrypted.
rules.remediation: Use https:// for any server that is not on the loopback interface, and authenticate the connection.

rules.title: MCP tools approved automatically
rules.message: The client is told to run this server's tools without asking a person.
rules.remediation: Remove the auto-approval, or limit it to named read-only tools. Keep human approval for any tool that writes, sends or deletes.

rules.title: Coding agent run with approvals or sandbox switched off
rules.message: A coding agent is started with its approval prompts or sandbox disabled.
rules.remediation: Run unattended agents only inside a disposable container with no production credentials and an egress allow-list, and keep the flag out of developer machines and shared scripts.
